tier1.text: Each hyoglossus muscle lowers and flattens the tongue. The hyoglossus also pulls the tongue back. Each hyoglossus runs from the hyoid bone, a U-shaped bone in the upper neck, to the side of the tongue. The hyoglossus is an extrinsic tongue muscle, which means it starts outside the tongue but attaches inside the tongue.

quotes.quote: The mylohyoid is responsible for raising the tongue, the hyoglossus pulls it down and back, the styloglossus pulls it up and back, and the genioglossus pulls it forward.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: A muscle extending from the hyoid bone to the side of the tongue that retracts and pulls the side of the tongue downward.
quotes.citation: NCI Thesaurus (NCIt), National Cancer Institute, https://ncithesaurus.nci.nih.gov

quotes.quote: hyoid bone: small, U-shaped bone located in upper neck that does not contact any other bone
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

quotes.quote: the extrinsic muscles of the tongue are the palatoglossus, hyoglossus, styloglossus, and genioglossus muscles. These muscles originate outside the tongue and insert into connective tissues within the tongue.
quotes.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
